claims.label: Wrongful Eviction / Unlawful Lockout
claims.note: No damages amount entered -- probability shown reflects state self-help law and whether statutory process was followed.

claims.label: Attorney's Fees
claims.note: Posture-tiered flat-dollar estimate (went to trial) -- fees are driven by procedural effort, not claim size, for a typical matter in this range; a large or unusually complex matter can run higher.

outcome.description: On partial summary judgment the court awarded $243,600 rent for March 2020 to May 2021, $17,052 interest and $6,701 utilities ($267,353; the procedural history swaps the interest and utilities labels, the damages section and conclusion confirm them). After the January 11, 2023 bench trial the court rejected the constructive-eviction defense, held double rent accrued only from August 1, 2021 after the July 28, 2021 notice, and awarded a further $431,861 rent and double rent for June 1, 2021 to September 21, 2022 and $67,381.33 interest at 1% per month on the balance excluding double rent, entering judgment for $766,595.33 ($675,461 rent, $84,433.33 interest, $6,701 utilities) plus post-judgment interest and attorney's fees to be set on motion.
outcome.finalNote: No appeal reflected in the source. Amount verified against the conclusion. It includes the 1%-per-month interest ($84,433.33) because the court awarded it as part of the damages and the landlord's own demands ($787,436.01 at trial) include it, as the set does for other lease judgments with contract-rate interest (e.g. GSL Investments, Slyce); without interest the award is $682,162. Fees awarded, amount not stated.

source.caseName: South Pacific Lumber Co. v. Imperial Pacific International (CNMI), LLC
source.court: U.S. District Court for the Northern Mariana Islands (findings of fact and conclusions of law after bench trial)
source.excerptNote: Verbatim from the introduction, Procedural History, Findings of Fact (lease, extension, access and padlocking, holdover notice) and, from the Conclusions of Law, only the parties' positions, the quoted HTA double-rent and fee provisions, the CNMI interest cap, SPLC's interest concession and the lease's fee clause. Kept: the court's pre-trial partial-summary-judgment liability rulings (no figures). Removed: the sentence stating the total awarded at trial and its components, the sentence stating the partial-summary-judgment dollar award, the court's finding that IPI always had access, the constructive-eviction holding, the double-rent accrual ruling, the interest ruling, the damages section and table, the conclusion, footnotes 1-7 (and footnote markers 1-4 dropped from their sentences), record citations in parentheses, PDF line numbers, page footers and the caption. Also removed in review: the finding that from June 8, 2022 'IPI had all the keys to use and access the Warehouse', which resolves the disputed constructive-eviction question.
